mainTopic: The שופר signal when יום הכיפורים is next to שבת, and whether trimming vegetables is allowed when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת
overview: רבי זירא reports that in בבל they thought a ברייתא was agreed by everyone. The ברייתא says that when יום הכיפורים is next to שבת, no שופר is blown and no הבדלה is made. In ארץ ישראל, יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי argued that it fits only רבי עקיבא. רבי זירא answered with כהנים זריזין הן, and the גמרא defended that answer: the מקדש blasts were for the rest of the people in ירושלים. The גמרא then asks why they do not blow when יום הכיפורים begins on מוצאי שבת, to tell people that trimming vegetables is permitted from מנחה. רב שישא says only a near שבות was permitted. That answer fails, because no שופר is blown even when יום טוב on מוצאי שבת makes שחיטה permitted right away. So the גמרא settles on רב יוסף: a שבות is not set aside just to announce a permission. Finally, רב הונא forbids and רבי יוחנן permits trimming vegetables when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, each reading the word שבתון differently. A ברייתא supporting רבי יוחנן begins and continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: In Babylonia they said the ברייתא is agreed by everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא recalls that in בבל they held that the ברייתא about no שופר and no הבדלה when יום הכיפורים touches שבת is accepted by all opinions.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I was in Babylonia we used to say: the ברייתא that teaches 'If יום הכיפורים falls on Friday, they would not blow the שופר, and on מוצאי שבת they would not make הבדלה' is the opinion of everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא quotes a ברייתא and reports how scholars in בבל understood it: as a ruling that every תנא agrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a שופר was blown on Friday afternoon to tell people to stop working, and הבדלה separates שבת from the next day. The ברייתא says neither happens when יום הכיפורים is right next to שבת. The Babylonian view is that this fits every opinion, even those who treat the holiness of the two days differently.

keyTerms.meaning: they make הבדלה (separate holy from holy or profane)
the words of everyone; all opinions agree

phrases.english: When I was in Babylonia
phrases.notes: The speaker in context is רבי זירא, who moved from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: we used to say:
that which was taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: יוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: If יום הכיפורים fell on Friday,
they would not blow the שופר,
phrases.notes: This refers to the usual Friday-afternoon blast announcing שבת.

phrases.english: and if it fell on מוצאי שבת, they would not make הבדלה,
this is the opinion of everyone.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא (no שופר, no הבדלה when יום הכיפורים is adjacent to שבת) is accepted by all תנאים.

steps.title: In ארץ ישראל: the ברייתא follows only רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בריה דרבי שמעון בן פזי argues that the ברייתא cannot fit רבי ישמעאל. In רבי ישמעאל's view the two days differ in holiness, so a שופר blast should mark the difference.
steps.simpleTranslation: When I went up there, to ארץ ישראל, I found יהודה, son of רבי שמעון בן פזי, sitting and saying: it is the view of רבי עקיבא. If it were רבי ישמעאל, then since he said that the fats of שבת offerings are brought on יום הכיפורים, they should blow, so that people will know that the fats of שבת are brought on יום הכיפורים.
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar in ארץ ישראל rejects the Babylonian claim that everyone agrees. He says the ברייתא matches only רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא treats יום הכיפורים and שבת as equally holy, so no blast or הבדלה is needed between them. רבי ישמעאל holds the two days are not equal, which is why he rules that the fats from שבת may be offered on יום הכיפורים. If the days are not equal, a שופר blast should announce that difference to the כהנים, so the ברייתא's 'no blowing' cannot fit רבי ישמעאל.

keyTerms.meaning: When I went up there (to ארץ ישראל)
the fats of the שבת offerings, burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a dispute about blowing שופר as a מצוה. The blast discussed here is a signal: an announcement that tells people something has changed between the days.

phrases.english: When I went up there,

phrases.aramaic: אַשְׁכְּחִיתֵיהּ לִיהוּדָה בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן פַּזִּי
phrases.english: I found Yehuda, son of Rabbi Shimon ben Pazi,
who was sitting and saying:
It is the view of Rabbi Akiva,
for if it were Rabbi Yishmael,
since he said
that the fats of Shabbat are offered on Yom Kippur,
let them blow,
so that they will know
that the fats of Shabbat are offered on Yom Kippur.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא הִיא, דְּאִי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the 'דברי הכל' claim of step 1 and limits the ברייתא to רבי עקיבא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that all תנאים agree with the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Under רבי ישמעאל the days differ in holiness, so a שופר signal would be needed, which contradicts the ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי זירא answers: the כהנים are quick and alert
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא defends the Babylonian view: the כהנים already know the law, so no שופר signal is needed even according to רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And I said to him: the כהנים are alert.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers יהודה's proof. The כהנים do not need a שופר to remind them of the law, so the ברייתא can still fit everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יהודה's proof assumed the blast was needed to inform the כהנים. רבי זירא denies that need, because the כהנים are expert and careful. Without that need, the reason to blow according to רבי ישמעאל disappears, and 'דברי הכל' stands again.

keyTerms.meaning: the כהנים are quick and careful

phrases.english: And I said to him:
The priests are vigilant.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמֵינָא לֵיהּ אֲנָא כֹּהֲנִים זְרִיזִין הֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 2 and restores the view of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the premise that a signal is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: According to רבי ישמעאל, a שופר is needed to inform the כהנים of the difference between the days.
steps.terutzMaskana: The כהנים are alert and know on their own, so no blast is needed, and the ברייתא can be דברי הכל.

steps.title: Challenge: the Temple blew blasts every Friday anyway
steps.stepSummary: מר קשישא challenges 'כהנים זריזין הן' from a משנה. Blasts were blown in the מקדש to stop work and to separate קודש from חול, which suggests signals were needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר קשישא, son of רב חסדא, said to רב אשי: Do we really say the כהנים are alert? But we learned in a משנה: three blasts to stop the people from work, and three blasts to separate between holy and ordinary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רבי זירא's answer. If the כהנים needed no reminders, why did the מקדש blow שופר blasts every Friday?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה describes six Friday blasts in the מקדש. These seem to be announcements, including for the כהנים serving there. That suggests the כהנים did rely on signals, which weakens 'כהנים זריזין הן'.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ מָר קַשִּׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב חִסְדָּא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Mar Kashisha, son of Rav Chisda, said to Rav Ashi:
Do we say that priests are vigilant?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
three blasts to stop the people from work,
three to separate between holy and ordinary.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי אָמְרִינַן כֹּהֲנִים זְרִיזִין הֵן? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 3.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows שופר signals were blown in the מקדש on Friday, implying the כהנים needed reminders.

steps.title: Answer: those blasts were for the rest of Jerusalem's people
steps.stepSummary: Using אביי's principle, the גמרא explains that the Friday blasts were meant for the general population of ירושלים, not for the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As אביי said elsewhere, it was for the rest of the people in ירושלים. Here too, the blasts were for the rest of the people in ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends 'כהנים זריזין הן' by saying the מקדש blasts were for ordinary people, not for the כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof from the משנה only works if the blasts were aimed at the כהנים. Borrowing אביי's line from another context, the גמרא says they were for the rest of ירושלים. So the כהנים can still be called alert, and רבי זירא's answer stands.

keyTerms.meaning: for the rest of the people

phrases.english: As Abaye said:
for the rest of the people in Jerusalem,
here too, for the rest of the people in Jerusalem.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the audience of the source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The Friday blasts in the מקדש were signals for the כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The blasts were for the general population of ירושלים, so כהנים זריזין הן remains true.
steps.whatToRemember: The rule כהנים זריזין הן survives. A שופר signal in the מקדש does not prove the כהנים needed reminders, because such blasts may be meant for the wider public.

steps.title: Challenge: blow anyway to announce vegetable trimming
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why they do not blow at the end of שבת when יום הכיפורים begins on מוצאי שבת. Such a blast would tell the public that, unlike on שבת, trimming vegetables is permitted on יום הכיפורים from מנחה time onward.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let them blow, so that people will know that trimming vegetables is permitted from מנחה time and onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new reason to blow the שופר. This blast would announce to the public that a certain preparation is now allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום הכיפורים, from מנחה time, one may trim vegetables to prepare for the meal after the fast. This is not allowed on שבת. When יום הכיפורים begins right as שבת ends, a blast could tell the public that the new day has a leniency שבת did not have. Since this blast would be for ordinary people, 'כהנים זריזין הן' does not answer it.

phrases.english: But let them blow,
so that they will know
that trimming vegetables is permitted
from the afternoon and onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After 'כהנים זריזין' is defended, the גמרא finds a public-facing reason to blow that the answer cannot cover.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that no signal was given when יום הכיפורים fell on מוצאי שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is a practical difference the public needs to know (vegetable trimming), so a signal should be blown.

steps.title: רב יוסף: a שבות is not set aside just to permit something
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that blowing the שופר is itself a rabbinic prohibition (שבות). It is not overridden merely to announce a permission.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: because we do not push aside a שבות in order to permit.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers the question of step 6. Blowing would break a rabbinic prohibition, and that is not allowed just to let people know something is permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blowing a שופר on יום הכיפורים or שבת is forbidden מדרבנן (a שבות). The trimming blast would serve only to announce a leniency, not to prevent any wrongdoing. חז"ל do not set aside a שבות for that purpose.

keyTerms.meaning: a rabbinic prohibition on שבת or יום טוב

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general limit: rabbinic restrictions are not suspended merely to announce a leniency.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Because a rabbinic prohibition is not overridden in order to permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף לְפִי שֶׁאֵין דּוֹחִין שְׁבוּת לְהַתִּיר
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A blast should be sounded to inform the public that vegetable trimming is permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: Blowing is a שבות, and a שבות is not overridden just to announce a permission.

steps.title: רב שישא: a near שבות was permitted, a distant one was not
steps.stepSummary: רב שישא בריה דרב אידי offers a different answer. חז"ל allowed blowing only when the permission applies right away, not for a permission that begins hours later.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב שישא, son of רב אידי, said: for a near שבות they permitted, but for a distant שבות they did not permit.
steps.whatsHappening: A second אמורא gives another answer to step 6, based on how close in time the permitted act is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שישא distinguishes by timing, not by the rule of 'never'. Blowing could be allowed when it announces something that takes effect immediately. Vegetable trimming is allowed only later, from מנחה, so its connection to the blast is too distant, and they did not permit blowing for it.

keyTerms.meaning: a near or immediate rabbinic matter
a distant or remote rabbinic matter

steps.whatToRemember: There are two answers for why no blast announces vegetable trimming. רב יוסף says a שבות is never overridden just to permit. רב שישא says only a near שבות was permitted, and trimming is too distant.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Sheisha, son of Rav Idi, said:
an immediate rabbinic prohibition, they permitted;
a remote rabbinic prohibition, they did not permit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב שִׁישָׁא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִידִי אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative resolution to the challenge of step 6, differing from רב יוסף.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any permission could justify blowing the שופר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a near, immediate matter justifies blowing. Vegetable trimming, permitted only from מנחה, is too distant.

steps.title: Challenge: no shofar even when slaughtering becomes permitted immediately
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב שישא's idea that חז"ל allow blowing for a permission that begins right away. A משנה says we do not blow when יום טוב begins on מוצאי שבת, even though שחיטה becomes permitted at that very moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did they really allow blowing for a permission that starts right away? We learned in a משנה: when יום טוב falls on Friday, we blow but do not make הבדלה. When it falls on Saturday night, we make הבדלה but do not blow. Why not blow then, so people know slaughtering is allowed immediately?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב שישא's answer from Step 8. It cites a case where a permission starts immediately, yet we still do not blow the שופר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When יום טוב begins on Saturday night, שחיטה moves from forbidden (שבת) to permitted (יום טוב) at that exact moment. According to רב שישא, that is exactly the kind of permission that should justify blowing. The משנה says we do not blow, so his rule seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic prohibition set aside for a permission that applies right away
We make הבדלה, marking the separation between levels of holiness
Ritual slaughter. It is forbidden on שבת and allowed on יום טוב for food.

steps.confusionAlert: On Friday יום טוב, the blasts announce שבת. There is no הבדלה because we are moving up to a holier day. On Saturday night we move down from שבת to יום טוב, so we make הבדלה. The question is only about why we do not also blow then.

phrases.english: And did they permit a rabbinic prohibition for an immediate permission?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָתְנַן: יוֹם טוֹב שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת —
phrases.english: But we learned: a Festival that falls on Shabbat eve —
one blows but does not make havdala.
On Saturday night, one makes havdala but does not blow.
phrases.notes: Here a יום טוב begins right as שבת ends.

phrases.english: But why? Let them blow,
so that people will know
that slaughtering is permitted immediately!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רב שישא's answer from Step 8
steps.kashyaTarget: רב שישא's rule that blowing is allowed for a permission that applies immediately
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: On מוצאי שבת that is יום טוב, שחיטה becomes permitted immediately, yet the משנה says we do not blow. That contradicts the proposed rule.

steps.title: Conclusion: the correct answer is רב יוסף's
steps.stepSummary: Since רב שישא's answer fails, the גמרא concludes that רב יוסף's explanation is the right one.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is clear that the answer follows רב יוסף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב שישא's answer and goes back to רב יוסף's answer from Step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said that blowing the שופר is a שבות. חז"ל never set it aside just to announce that something has become permitted, whether the permission starts later or right away. That explains both cases: no blast when יום הכיפורים begins on מוצאי שבת (trimming vegetables), and no blast when יום טוב begins on מוצאי שבת (שחיטה).

keyTerms.meaning: It is clear. The גמרא uses this word to settle on one explanation after another one fails.

steps.whatToRemember: We do not blow the שופר just to announce a permission. Blowing is a שבות, and it is not set aside for that purpose (רב יוסף).

phrases.english: Rather, it is clear that it is like Rav Yosef.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the problem from Step 9 by returning to Step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף's explanation stands: the שבות of blowing is not set aside to announce a permission.

steps.title: רב הונא: trimming vegetables is forbidden when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת
steps.stepSummary: A new statement: when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, קניבת ירק is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רב הונא (some say רבי אבא said it in the name of רב הונא): when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, trimming vegetables is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new discussion about trimming vegetables when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת. רב הונא rules that it is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (Step 6) we saw that on a weekday יום הכיפורים, trimming vegetables is allowed from מנחה time. רב הונא says that when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, this permission does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: Trimming vegetables, meaning removing the outer leaves to prepare them for eating

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rav Huna said,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: and some say Rabbi Abba said that Rav Huna said:
Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat —
trimming vegetables is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the שופר discussion to the trimming-vegetables topic raised in Step 6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, קניבת ירק is forbidden.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the prohibition from the word שבתון
steps.stepSummary: רב מנא cites a ברייתא that learns the prohibition from the word שבתון, which it reads as שבות, a rest even from non-מלאכה activities.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנא said that a ברייתא taught: how do we know that when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, trimming vegetables is forbidden? The verse says שבתון, which means שבות.
steps.whatsHappening: רב מנא brings a ברייתא that supports רב הונא. It points to the extra word שבתון in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the word שבתון as a signal that there is an extra level of rest, called שבות. The גמרא will next ask what that extra rest is meant to cover.

keyTerms.meaning: A word in the פסוק meaning 'solemn rest'

phrases.english: Rav Mana said: It was taught:

phrases.aramaic: מִנַּיִן לְיוֹם הַכִּיפּוּרִים שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת
phrases.english: From where do we know that Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat
is forbidden for trimming vegetables?
The verse says: "Shabbaton", meaning a rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides a source for רב הונא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's ruling that קניבת ירק is forbidden
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that learns it from the word שבתון

steps.title: What does the extra rest refer to?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what שבתון comes to forbid. It cannot mean real מלאכה, because the Torah already forbids that explicitly.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what is this rest? If you say for real מלאכה, it is already written: 'Do not do any work'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move. It asks what שבתון adds and rules out the simple answer that it means real מלאכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A word in the Torah should teach something new. מלאכה is already forbidden by 'לא תעשה כל מלאכה', so שבתון must be teaching something beyond that.

phrases.english: For what? If you say for labor —
but it is written: "You shall not do any labor"!

steps.sheelahInformationSought: What new prohibition does שבתון add?

steps.title: So שבתון must refer to trimming vegetables
steps.stepSummary: Since שבתון cannot mean real מלאכה, it must refer to trimming vegetables. The גמרא accepts this proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, is it not about trimming vegetables? Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the reasoning: the extra word must forbid trimming vegetables. It accepts the proof with 'שמע מינה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By ruling out real מלאכה, the only option left is a lighter activity like קניבת ירק. This confirms רב הונא's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it. This accepts a proof.

phrases.english: Rather, is it not about trimming vegetables!
Learn from it.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to this ברייתא, שבתון forbids קניבת ירק when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: trimming vegetables is permitted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן disagrees with רב הונא and rules that trimming vegetables is permitted when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, trimming vegetables is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an opposing view: רבי יוחנן permits trimming vegetables in this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a direct disagreement with רב הונא in Step 11. Because the ברייתא we just saw seems to support רב הונא, a challenge to רבי יוחנן is coming next.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya bar Abba said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Yom Kippur that falls on Shabbat —
trimming vegetables is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents the opposite view to רב הונא
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, קניבת ירק is permitted.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי יוחנן from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן from the same ברייתא, which seems to forbid trimming vegetables based on שבתון.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: how do we know that when יום הכיפורים falls on שבת, trimming vegetables is forbidden? The verse says שבתון, meaning rest. For what? If for real מלאכה, it is already written 'Do not do any work.' So it must be about trimming vegetables!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the ברייתא and its reasoning, this time as an attack on רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same words that supported רב הונא now contradict רבי יוחנן. If שבתון must mean something other than מלאכה, then trimming vegetables is forbidden.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a pointless repeat. The same ברייתא is quoted again for a new purpose: to attack רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: They objected: From where do we know that Yom Kippur

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁחָל לִהְיוֹת בְּשַׁבָּת שֶׁאָסוּר בִּקְנִיבַת יָרָק —
phrases.english: that falls on Shabbat is forbidden for trimming vegetables?
The verse says: "Shabbaton", meaning a rest.
For what? If you say for labor —
but it is written: "You shall not do any labor"
Rather, is it not about trimming vegetables!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יוחנן's ruling in Step 15
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's permission to trim vegetables
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא reads שבתון as forbidding something beyond מלאכה, which must be קניבת ירק.

steps.title: שבתון adds a positive commandment against real מלאכה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's side answers that שבתון does refer to real מלאכה. It adds a positive commandment (עשה), so someone who does מלאכה breaks both an עשה and a לא תעשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. It really refers to מלאכה, and it teaches that one who does it violates both a positive commandment and a prohibition.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן by reading שבתון differently. It still refers to real מלאכה, but it adds an extra commandment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that שבתון must teach a new prohibited activity. The answer shows it can teach something new about the same activity: an added עשה on top of the לאו. So the word is not extra, and trimming vegetables is not forbidden by it.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really. It introduces the answer's true reading.

phrases.english: No, it actually refers to labor,
to make one violate both a positive commandment and a prohibition for it.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: שבתון must forbid a new activity beyond מלאכה, namely קניבת ירק
steps.terutzMaskana: שבתון adds an עשה to the existing לאו against מלאכה, so קניבת ירק stays permitted

steps.deeperAnalysis: After defending רבי יוחנן, the גמרא now brings positive support for his view. The actual ruling of the ברייתא appears right on the next עמוד.
